  • The intervals hold, and are wide for their label. 60 of the 80 lists fell inside their 60% intervals, three in four, against the 48 that intervals at that level would catch (give or take 4): the list error of 5.5 is generous, so the band holds more often than its label says.
  • The threshold calls are good in six elections, Brier scores of 0.01–0.09, and poor in April 2019 (0.19): New Right and Zehut, polled at five or six seats each, were given better-than-even chances of passing and both failed.
  • The Netanyahu bloc's result fell inside its interval in all seven elections. The chance given to 61 or more was 77% in 2013 (it won 61), 54% in April 2019 (65) and 66% in 2022 (64), and 4–18% in the four elections it fell short.
  • The correction costs coverage at this level: 60 lists inside with it against 63 without, Brier 0.067 against 0.066. Moving the Right's surplus to Likud brings two more lists inside in April 2019 and one in 2015, and improves the threshold calls in 2015; it takes three out in 2021, where the surplus went to the centre instead, and two in 2022. The 2015 fold also corrects the Haredi parties and the 2021 fold the Left: the rule's choice of families is not stable from fold to fold, which is why the seven-election rule keeps only the Right.

The point accuracy is the polls' own (section 5): the simulation does not make the centre better, it puts honest error bars around it. A median is also a poor point estimate for a list near the threshold, which either wins nothing or wins four seats: Ra'am 2021 passed in fewer than half the draws, so its median was 0.

The chart shows every list with the correction.

The eight misses outside the intervals are the big late moves the final polls did not see: Yesh Atid in 2013 (polled 11, won 19) and the Likud–Yisrael Beiteinu list that lost those votes; Likud in 2015 (median 23, won 30); Likud and Blue and White in April 2019, both 35 against medians of 31 and 29; and in 2021 Blue and White (polled 4, won 8), New Hope (10, won 6) and Likud, a miss the correction created by giving Likud a surplus that went to the centre that year. A model built on the final polls cannot see a late swing the polls did not see.

7.3 Combining the polls and the flow model¶

Two forecasts of the same election: the polls (opinion today, with known errors) and the flow model (each place's recent vote with 2026's population, which misses whatever has changed since). Weighting each by the inverse of its error variance gives the combination with the smallest expected error, if the two errors are independent.

  • The polls' error: the back-test shares of 7.2 (with the correction) against the results of the seven elections, by camp: the right-religious families, the centre-left with Yisrael Beiteinu, and the Arab lists.
  • The flow model's error: each camp's share carried forward one election, for every pair from 2015 to 2022 (2013 is left out: Yisrael Beiteinu ran inside Likud's list then). This error grows with the time between elections, so it is measured per year (variance divided by the years between the two elections) and scaled to the four years from 2022 to 2026.
In [57]:
CAMPS = {"Right-religious": ["Likud", "Right", "Haredi"], "Centre-left": ["Centre", "Left", "Yisrael Beiteinu"],
         "Arab lists": ["Arab lists"]}
family_share = list_votes.pivot_table(index="election", columns="family", values="share_pct", aggfunc="sum").fillna(0)
camp_share = pd.DataFrame({c: family_share[f].sum(axis=1) for c, f in CAMPS.items()})

carried = pd.DataFrame([{"from": ELECTIONS.loc[a, "label"], "to": ELECTIONS.loc[b, "label"],
                         "years": (ELECTIONS.loc[b, "date"] - ELECTIONS.loc[a, "date"]).days / 365.25,
                         **(camp_share.loc[a] - camp_share.loc[b]).to_dict()}
                        for a, b in zip(order[1:-1], order[2:])])
HORIZON_2026 = (ELECTION_DAY_2026 - ELECTIONS.loc["K25", "date"]).days / 365.25
flow_variance = (carried[list(CAMPS)] ** 2).sum() / carried["years"].sum() * HORIZON_2026

poll_camp_errors = {}
for e in PAST:
    family = list_votes[list_votes["election"] == e].set_index("list")["family"]
    poll = backtests[(e, True)]["shares"].drop("others")
    poll_camp = pd.Series({c: poll[family.reindex(poll.index).isin(f).to_numpy()].sum() for c, f in CAMPS.items()})
    poll_camp_errors[ELECTIONS.loc[e, "label"]] = poll_camp - camp_share.loc[e]
poll_variance = (pd.DataFrame(poll_camp_errors).T ** 2).mean()

POLL_WEIGHT = float(flow_variance.mean() / (poll_variance.mean() + flow_variance.mean()))
display(carried.round(2))
print(f"Weight on the polls: {POLL_WEIGHT:.2f}; on the flow model: {1 - POLL_WEIGHT:.2f}")
pd.DataFrame({"polls: error sd": np.sqrt(poll_variance),
              "flow model: error sd at 4 years": np.sqrt(flow_variance)}).round(2)

Carried forward over four years, a camp's share misses by 3.7–4.6 points (one standard deviation); the polls model, back-tested on seven elections, missed by 1.9–2.9 points. The weights come out at 78% for the polls and 22% for the flow model, and the combination gives the Netanyahu bloc 55 seats before any uncertainty is added: between the corrected polls' 54 and the flow model's 58.

Two caveats. The flow model's error rests mostly on elections less than two years apart, scaled up by an assumption (error variance growing in proportion to the time between elections), and the polls' camp errors are measured on shares rebuilt from seats. The single-model and equal-weight forecasts are in 7.5.

    return POLL_WEIGHT * polls + (1 - POLL_WEIGHT) * flow_2026.reindex(polls.index)

  • No bloc reaches 61 in most simulated elections. The Netanyahu bloc's median is 55 seats (60% interval 51–59), and it reaches 61 in 11% of the draws, about one in nine.
  • The opposition alone reaches 61 in 3% of the draws. With the Arab lists it does in 84%: a majority without the Netanyahu bloc depends on the Arab lists in almost every draw.
  • Likud is the largest list, 25 seats (23–27), ahead of Yashar! with 21 (20–23). The correction of 5.2 is worth about two of Likud's seats.
  • Ra'am passes in 77% of the draws, Hendel and Zelekha in 45%, Amkha Yisrael in 37%.

What the threshold lists decide¶

Two lists sit just under the threshold, one in each camp: Amkha Yisrael counts in the Netanyahu bloc, Hendel and Zelekha in the opposition. The draws split four ways by which of them passes.

7.5 Sensitivity¶

The forecast rests on choices made in sections 5–7. Each row below changes one of them and reruns the 20,000 draws with the same random numbers, so the differences are the effect of that choice alone.

  • Polls only, flow only, equal weights: the two models alone, and an even split instead of the weight of 7.3.
  • No poll correction: the polls as published, combined with the flow model.
  • Right surplus shared by all lists: the Right's 2.0 points taken away as in 5.2, but spread over every other list by size instead of given to Likud.
  • Bloc swing: a shared error moving votes between the Netanyahu bloc and the opposition, with a standard deviation of one list error (1.6 points). Its size is hand-set; 5.5 found no shared swing to measure.
  • Polls weighted by sample size: every poll of the final week, weighted by its respondents (section 5.4).
  • Arab turnout as in 2021 or 2020: the Arab lists' total share from the turnout model of section 6 at that election's Arab turnout, split between the Joint List and Ra'am as in the polls, and the other lists rescaled.
In [66]:
def poll_shares(rows):
    """Each poll's list shares summing to 100 with "others", Blue and White folded into the opposition."""
    raw = rows[share_columns].fillna(0)
    raw.columns = [c.removesuffix("_pct") for c in raw.columns]
    out = raw.div(raw.sum(axis=1), axis=0) * 100
    withdrawn = out.pop("blue_white")
    out[opposition] += out[opposition].mul(withdrawn / out[opposition].sum(axis=1), axis=0)
    out["others"] = out.drop(columns=on_ballot).sum(axis=1)
    return out[list(on_ballot) + ["others"]]


assert np.allclose(poll_shares(with_shares.reset_index()).mean(), average_2026[list(on_ballot) + ["others"]])

week = k26[(k26["date"] > k26["date"].max() - pd.Timedelta(days=7)) & k26[share_columns].notna().any(axis=1)]
weighted_2026 = poll_shares(week).mul(week["respondents"].to_numpy(), axis=0).sum() / week["respondents"].sum()


def with_arab_turnout(shares, turnout):
    """The Arab lists' total share from the turnout model, split as in the polls; the other lists rescaled."""
    target = sector_model({**PARAMS_2026, "turnout_arab": turnout})["arab_lists_share"]
    arab = ["joint_list", "raam"]
    out = shares.copy()
    out[arab] *= target / shares[arab].sum()
    rest = shares.index.difference(arab)
    out[rest] *= (100 - target) / shares[rest].sum()
    return out


def run_scenario(shares, **options):
    _, seats = simulate(shares, AGREEMENTS_2026, n=FORECAST_DRAWS, **options)
    totals = seats.drop(columns="others").T.groupby(BLOC_2026).sum().T
    return {"Netanyahu": totals["Netanyahu"].median(),
            f"Netanyahu {INTERVAL}%": f"{totals['Netanyahu'].quantile(LOW):.0f}–{totals['Netanyahu'].quantile(HIGH):.0f}",
            "Opposition": totals["Opposition"].median(), "Arab lists": totals["Arab lists"].median(),
            "P(Netanyahu 61+)": (totals["Netanyahu"] >= 61).mean(),
            "P(Opposition + Arab 61+)": ((totals["Opposition"] + totals["Arab lists"]) >= 61).mean()}

  • The weight on the flow model matters most. Polls alone give the Netanyahu bloc 54 seats and a 7% chance of 61; equal weights 57 and 19%; the flow model alone 59 and 41%.
  • Every variant but the flow model alone leaves the bloc short of 61 in most draws; its chance of 61 runs from 6% to 23%.
  • How the polls are averaged matters next. Weighting them by sample size gives Next Data, the pollster with by far the largest Likud, 44% of the weight among the polls that print shares: the bloc's median rises to 57 and its chance of 61 to 23%.
  • Arab turnout moves the Arab lists two to three seats each way: 11 at 2021's turnout (the bloc 56, a 17% chance of 61), 16 at 2020's (the bloc 54, 6%).
  • The poll correction is worth a seat and a few points of probability: 54 seats and a 9% chance without it, 7% with the Right's surplus shared over all lists instead of moved to Likud. The bloc swing adds spread, not seats (14%).

7.6 The forecast in one paragraph¶

On the polls of 15–21 October, corrected for the final polls' habit since 2013 of overstating the parties to Likud's right at Likud's expense, and combined with a flow model of every polling place (78% polls, 22% flow), the Netanyahu bloc wins about 55 seats (60% interval 51–59) and reaches 61 in about one simulated election in nine. The opposition and the Arab lists together win about 65. The largest uncertainties are how much weight the flow model deserves, the two lists just under the threshold, and how the polls are averaged.

8. Limitations and scoring after the election¶

8.1 Limitations¶

  • Seats-only polls. The 2013–2022 polls publish seats, not vote shares, so the shares behind them are rebuilt from the seats (7.2), and a list a pollster shows under the threshold counts as nothing. The 2026 run uses the printed shares, so the back-test checks a slightly different input.
  • The correction is one pattern, aimed at Likud. The Right's surplus is moved to Likud because that is where it went in 2015 and April 2019; in 2021 it went to the centre, and the back-test's 2021 fold is worse with the correction than without. In 2026 the Right family includes Beyahad, an opposition list, so the correction also moves 0.8 points across the blocs. The rule's choice of families moves between folds (the Haredi parties in the 2015 fold, the Left in the 2021 fold).
  • The Haredi lean is left in. The Haredi parties are under-polled in six of the seven elections, by 0.7 points on average, under the rule's one-seat bar; a correction would be worth about a seat to the bloc.
  • The polls carry most of the weight. The model corrects one known bias and adds a flow model at 22%, but it cannot see a late shift the polls miss, as with Likud in 2015 or Blue and White in 2021.
  • The flow model's camps. It carries 2022's Likud, Religious Zionism and centre votes into today's lists and splits them between the new lists by the polls, so who Beyahad or Yashar! take their voters from is an assumption.
  • The weight between the two models rests on seven elections of polls and five pairs of elections for the flow model, most of them less than two years apart, scaled to four years by assumption.
  • Independent list errors. Lists of one camp may be missed together. The seven elections show no shared bloc swing beyond what independent errors produce (5.5), and the bloc-swing sensitivity covers it only roughly, at a hand-set size.
  • One error size for every list. A list at 3% gets the same 1.6-point error as one at 17%, which piles draws at zero for the small lists and makes the intervals of the large ones wide for their label: the back-test's 60% intervals caught 75% of the results.
  • No pollster house effects. The pollsters disagree widely in 2026 (Likud 18–30 seats), and the average gives each one vote; section 7.5 shows how much the weighting matters.
  • Turnout. The roll forecast overshot the published 2026 roll by 1% (2.7% in the Arab sector), voters living abroad enter only as a lever of the scenario (9), and Arab turnout enters through the polls, the flow model's place averages and the scenarios.
  • The polls end on 21 October, six days before the election.

8.2 Scoring after the election¶

Once the CEC publishes the results, this section scores the forecast against them, with the poll average as published as the baseline:

  • per list: how many results fall inside their 60% intervals, the seat error, and the Brier score of each list's chance of passing the threshold;
  • the bloc: the Netanyahu bloc's result against its forecast interval, and the probability the forecast gave to what happened (61 or more, or not).

To run it:

  1. Save the CEC's results by locality as data/cec_results/k26_2026/results_by_town.csv, converted to UTF-8 like the other years.
  2. Fill in LETTERS_2026 with each list's ballot letters from the CEC's list of the 2026 lists.
  3. Run the notebook.

The 2026 seats are counted with bader_ofer and the five 2026 surplus agreements of data/lists_2026.csv.

In [68]:
def score_forecast(seats, actual, bloc, baseline):
    """Scores simulated seats (draws x lists) against the actual seats, next to a baseline seat count."""
    lists = actual.index
    draws = seats[lists]
    low, high, median, passes = draws.quantile(LOW), draws.quantile(HIGH), draws.median(), (draws > 0).mean()
    side = bloc.reindex(lists)
    bloc_draws = draws.T.groupby(side).sum().T["Netanyahu"]
    bloc_actual = actual.groupby(side).sum()["Netanyahu"]
    p61 = (bloc_draws >= 61).mean()
    return pd.DataFrame({
        "forecast": {
            f"results inside the {INTERVAL}% interval": f"{((actual >= low) & (actual <= high)).sum()} of {len(lists)}",
            "seat error per list (median)": f"{(median - actual).abs().mean():.2f}",
            "Brier score, pass or fail": f"{((passes - (actual > 0)) ** 2).mean():.3f}",
            "Netanyahu bloc, forecast against result":
                f"{bloc_draws.median():.0f} ({bloc_draws.quantile(LOW):.0f}–{bloc_draws.quantile(HIGH):.0f}) vs {bloc_actual}",
            "probability given to what happened": f"{(p61 if bloc_actual >= 61 else 1 - p61):.0%}"},
        "polls as published": {
            f"results inside the {INTERVAL}% interval": "–",
            "seat error per list (median)": f"{(baseline[lists] - actual).abs().mean():.2f}",
            "Brier score, pass or fail": f"{(((baseline[lists] > 0).astype(float) - (actual > 0)) ** 2).mean():.3f}",
            "Netanyahu bloc, forecast against result": f"{baseline[lists].groupby(side).sum()['Netanyahu']:.0f} vs {bloc_actual}",
            "probability given to what happened": "–"},
    })

9. The scenario: hand-set turnouts on the 2026 electorate¶

The main forecast carries turnout from the past: the polls' respondents and each polling place's recent turnout. This section replaces it with expectations set by hand, one for each of three groups of voters, applied to the 2026 electorate from the growth trends of 6.2. The turnouts are beliefs, not estimates from the data; each is shown next to its 2022 value so that the reader can judge it.

How the scenario is built:

  1. The electorate. The 2026 roll by group from the growth trends of 6.2: Haredi voters growing 4.5% a year, the Arab sector 3.1%, other Jewish voters 1.5%. The forecast roll is 1% above the published 2026 roll in total and 2.7% above it in the Arab sector (6.1); the table below shows both.
  2. The votes. Each group's roll times its turnout, less 2022's invalid rate: the Arab sector with its double envelopes as in 6.3, the Haredi group at the ballot boxes, the other Jewish voters with the rest of the double envelopes. This is the two-sector model of 6.3 with the Haredi boxes (6.2's definition: the Haredi lists at 60% or more of the vote) taken out of the Jewish sector.
  3. Who gets them. The Arab lists take their loyalty share of the Arab sector's vote and 2022's small shares of the other two groups. The Haredi lists take 2022's share of the Haredi group's vote and of the other Jewish vote. These two totals replace the main forecast's; every other list takes what is left in the main forecast's proportions, so the polls still decide the centre and Likud. The Joint List and Ra'am split as set below, Shas and UTJ as in the main forecast.
  4. The simulation. 20,000 elections as in 7.4: each draws its own turnouts and loyalty, uniform within the ranges set, and every list gets the poll error of 5.5.

The settings:

Setting What it does None means
arab_turnout Arab turnout at the ballot boxes, %, a value or a (low, high) range –
haredi_turnout turnout at the Haredi boxes, % –
jewish_turnout other Jewish turnout with the double envelopes, % –
arab_loyalty % of the Arab sector's valid votes that go to the Arab lists –
haredi_loyalty % of the Haredi group's valid votes that go to Shas and UTJ 2022's
joint_list_share the Joint List's % of the two Arab lists' votes the main forecast's split
poll_weight % weight of the polls against the flow model the weight of 7.3 (78%)
list_adjustments share points added to or taken from lists, e.g. {"likud": 1.0, "yashar": -1.0} no change
voters_abroad thousand citizens on the roll who live abroad; the turnouts above are shares of the roll with 810 –
abroad_split % of the voters abroad in each group, hand-set –
In [71]:
THREE_GROUPS = ["Arab sector", "Haredi", "Other Jewish"]


def group_parameters_2022():
    """The three-group turnout model as it was in 2022: each group's roll, turnout and invalid rate, and the share
    of each group's valid votes that went to the Arab lists and to the Haredi lists."""
    g = (boxes[boxes["election"] == "K25"].groupby("growth_group")
              [["registered", "voted", "invalid", "valid", "Haredi", "Arab lists"]].sum())
    h, total = history.loc["K25"], national.loc["K25"]
    votes = list_votes[list_votes["election"] == "K25"].groupby("family")["votes"].sum()
    ballots_arab = g.loc["Arab sector", "registered"] * h["turnout_arab"] * h["envelope_factor"]
    valid_arab = ballots_arab * (1 - h["invalid_arab"])
    valid_haredi = g.loc["Haredi", "valid"]
    ballots_other = total["voted"] - ballots_arab - g.loc["Haredi", "voted"]
    valid_other = total["valid"] - valid_arab - valid_haredi
    p = {"roll_arab": g.loc["Arab sector", "registered"], "turnout_arab": h["turnout_arab"],
         "envelope_factor": h["envelope_factor"], "invalid_arab": h["invalid_arab"], "loyalty": h["loyalty"],
         "haredi_in_arab": g.loc["Arab sector", "Haredi"] / g.loc["Arab sector", "valid"],
         "roll_haredi": g.loc["Haredi", "registered"],
         "turnout_haredi": g.loc["Haredi", "voted"] / g.loc["Haredi", "registered"],
         "invalid_haredi": g.loc["Haredi", "invalid"] / g.loc["Haredi", "voted"],
         "haredi_loyalty": g.loc["Haredi", "Haredi"] / valid_haredi,
         "arab_in_haredi": g.loc["Haredi", "Arab lists"] / valid_haredi,
         "roll_other": g.loc["Other Jewish", "registered"],
         "turnout_other": ballots_other / g.loc["Other Jewish", "registered"],
         "invalid_other": 1 - valid_other / ballots_other}
    p["haredi_in_other"] = (votes["Haredi"] - p["haredi_loyalty"] * valid_haredi - p["haredi_in_arab"] * valid_arab) / valid_other
    p["arab_in_other"] = (votes["Arab lists"] - p["loyalty"] * valid_arab - p["arab_in_haredi"] * valid_haredi) / valid_other
    return pd.Series(p)


def group_model(p):
    """Valid votes, and the Arab lists' and Haredi lists' shares of them, for one setting or for arrays of them."""
    valid_arab = p["roll_arab"] * p["turnout_arab"] * p["envelope_factor"] * (1 - p["invalid_arab"])
    valid_haredi = p["roll_haredi"] * p["turnout_haredi"] * (1 - p["invalid_haredi"])
    valid_other = p["roll_other"] * p["turnout_other"] * (1 - p["invalid_other"])
    valid = valid_arab + valid_haredi + valid_other
    arab_lists = p["loyalty"] * valid_arab + p["arab_in_haredi"] * valid_haredi + p["arab_in_other"] * valid_other
    haredi_lists = p["haredi_loyalty"] * valid_haredi + p["haredi_in_arab"] * valid_arab + p["haredi_in_other"] * valid_other
    return {"valid": valid, "arab_lists_share": 100 * arab_lists / valid, "haredi_lists_share": 100 * haredi_lists / valid}


GROUP_2022 = group_parameters_2022()
replay_2022 = group_model(GROUP_2022)
family_2022 = 100 * list_votes[list_votes["election"] == "K25"].groupby("family")["votes"].sum() / national.loc["K25", "valid"]
assert np.isclose(replay_2022["valid"], national.loc["K25", "valid"])
assert np.isclose(replay_2022["arab_lists_share"], family_2022["Arab lists"])
assert np.isclose(replay_2022["haredi_lists_share"], family_2022["Haredi"])

    "haredi_turnout": 75,            # % at all Haredi boxes; hand-set belief (2022: 73.5, 2013–2022 average 74.6)

    "poll_weight": None,             # % weight of the polls against the flow model; None = 7.3's
    "list_adjustments": {},          # share points added to or taken from lists
    "voters_abroad": 810,            # thousand citizens on the roll who live abroad; CBS, October 2026 (7.3 million on the roll, 6.5 in Israel)
    "abroad_split": {"Arab sector": 5, "Haredi": 5, "Other Jewish": 90},   # % of them by group; hand-set, the CBS gives no split
}
VOTERS_ABROAD_2026 = 810             # the turnouts above are shares of the roll as published, which carries these voters
GROUP_KEYS = {"Arab sector": "arab", "Haredi": "haredi", "Other Jewish": "other"}
ARAB, HAREDI = ["joint_list", "raam"], ["shas", "utj"]


def setting(value, rng=None, n=1):
    """A number as it is; a (low, high) range as its midpoint, or as n uniform draws when rng is given."""
    if np.isscalar(value):
        return np.full(n, float(value))
    low, high = value
    return rng.uniform(low, high, n) if rng is not None else np.full(n, (low + high) / 2)


def abroad_factors(s):
    """Turnout multipliers by group when s["voters_abroad"] thousand voters are abroad instead of 2026's 810: anyone
    not abroad after all votes at the rate of the voters present, so a group's turnout of the roll rises with its
    share of the returning voters."""
    f = {}
    for group, key in GROUP_KEYS.items():
        roll, share = GROUP_2026[f"roll_{key}"], 1000 * s["abroad_split"][group] / 100
        f[key] = (1 - s["voters_abroad"] * share / roll) / (1 - VOTERS_ABROAD_2026 * share / roll)
    return f


def scenario_base(s):
    """The main forecast's shares at the chosen poll weight, with the list adjustments."""
    weight = POLL_WEIGHT if s["poll_weight"] is None else s["poll_weight"] / 100
    shares = weight * corrected_2026 + (1 - weight) * flow_2026.reindex(corrected_2026.index)
    for key, points in s["list_adjustments"].items():
        shares[key] += points
    shares = shares.clip(lower=0)
    return 100 * shares / shares.sum()


def scenario_matrix(s, rng=None, n=1):
    """n settings of the scenario as a share matrix (n x lists): the Arab and Haredi totals from the three-group
    model, the other lists filling what is left in the main forecast's proportions."""
    base, f = scenario_base(s), abroad_factors(s)
    p = {**GROUP_2026, "turnout_arab": f["arab"] * setting(s["arab_turnout"], rng, n) / 100,
         "turnout_haredi": f["haredi"] * setting(s["haredi_turnout"], rng, n) / 100,
         "turnout_other": f["other"] * setting(s["jewish_turnout"], rng, n) / 100,
         "loyalty": setting(s["arab_loyalty"], rng, n) / 100}
    if s["haredi_loyalty"] is not None:
        p["haredi_loyalty"] = setting(s["haredi_loyalty"], rng, n) / 100
    model = group_model(p)
    joint = base["joint_list"] / base[ARAB].sum() if s["joint_list_share"] is None else s["joint_list_share"] / 100
    shas = base["shas"] / base[HAREDI].sum()
    index = base.index
    rest = ~index.isin(ARAB + HAREDI + ["others"])
    out = np.tile(base.to_numpy(float), (n, 1))
    out[:, rest] *= ((100 - base["others"] - model["arab_lists_share"] - model["haredi_lists_share"]) / base[rest].sum())[:, None]
    out[:, index.get_loc("joint_list")] = model["arab_lists_share"] * joint
    out[:, index.get_loc("raam")] = model["arab_lists_share"] * (1 - joint)
    out[:, index.get_loc("shas")] = model["haredi_lists_share"] * shas
    out[:, index.get_loc("utj")] = model["haredi_lists_share"] * (1 - shas)
    return pd.DataFrame(out, columns=index)


def scenario_draws(s, n=FORECAST_DRAWS, seed=2026):
    """Simulated elections: each with its own turnouts and loyalty, and the poll error on every list."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    shares = scenario_matrix(s, rng, n)
    error = LIST_ERROR_POINTS * (shares.columns != "others").astype(float)
    drawn = np.clip(shares.to_numpy() + rng.normal(0, 1, shares.shape) * error, 0, None)
    drawn = 100 * drawn / drawn.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    seats = bader_ofer_fast(drawn, agreement_units(shares.columns, AGREEMENTS_2026), 3.25)
    return pd.DataFrame(drawn, columns=shares.columns), pd.DataFrame(seats, columns=shares.columns)


scenario_2026 = scenario_matrix(SCENARIO).iloc[0]                       # the midpoint setting, before any error
_, scenario_seats = scenario_draws(SCENARIO)
scenario_lists, _, scenario_totals = summarize(scenario_seats, BLOC_2026)
scenario_totals["Opposition + Arab lists"] = scenario_totals["Opposition"] + scenario_totals["Arab lists"]

print(f"Arab lists: {scenario_2026[ARAB].sum():.2f}% of the vote in the scenario, {blended_2026[ARAB].sum():.2f}% in the main "
      f"forecast; Haredi lists: {scenario_2026[HAREDI].sum():.2f}% against {blended_2026[HAREDI].sum():.2f}%")

Arab lists: 13.90% of the vote in the scenario, 10.96% in the main forecast; Haredi lists: 14.19% against 12.43%

Fewer voters abroad¶

The roll carries about 810,000 citizens who live abroad (CBS, October 2026: 7.3 million on the roll, 6.5 million of them in Israel), and only envoys and diplomats can vote from there. Every turnout in this notebook, past or hand-set, is a share of that roll. The lever voters_abroad asks what changes if fewer are abroad than the CBS counts, or if some return to vote: anyone not abroad after all votes at the rate of the voters present, so each group's turnout of the roll rises by its share of the returning voters. The CBS publishes no split by group, so abroad_split is hand-set: 90% other Jewish voters, 5% Arab, 5% Haredi.

def scenario_summary(s):
    """One setting of the scenario: its turnouts of the roll, central shares and simulated medians."""
    central, f = scenario_matrix(s).iloc[0], abroad_factors(s)
    _, seats = scenario_draws(s)
    _, _, totals = summarize(seats, BLOC_2026)
    return {"voters abroad (thousand)": s["voters_abroad"],
            "Arab turnout %": f["arab"] * np.mean(s["arab_turnout"]),
            "Haredi turnout %": f["haredi"] * np.mean(s["haredi_turnout"]),
            "other Jewish turnout %": f["other"] * np.mean(s["jewish_turnout"]),
            "Arab lists %": central[ARAB].sum(), "Haredi lists %": central[HAREDI].sum(),
            "Netanyahu": totals["Netanyahu"].median(), "P(61+)": (totals["Netanyahu"] >= 61).mean(),
            "Opposition": totals["Opposition"].median(), "Arab lists": totals["Arab lists"].median(),
            "Joint List": seats["joint_list"].median(), "Ra'am": seats["raam"].median(),
            "Opposition + Arab lists": (totals["Opposition"] + totals["Arab lists"]).median()}


abroad_table = (pd.DataFrame([scenario_summary({**SCENARIO, "voters_abroad": k}) for k in (810, 700, 600, 500)])
                  .set_index("voters abroad (thousand)"))
display(abroad_table.style.format("{:.0f}").format("{:.1f}", subset=[c for c in abroad_table.columns if "turnout" in c])
                    .format("{:.2f}", subset=["Arab lists %", "Haredi lists %"]).format("{:.1%}", subset=["P(61+)"]))

roll_total = sum(GROUP_2026[f"roll_{k}"] for k in GROUP_KEYS.values())
bounds = {"all of them other Jewish voters": {"Arab sector": 0, "Haredi": 0, "Other Jewish": 100},
          "split in proportion to the rolls": {g: 100 * GROUP_2026[f"roll_{k}"] / roll_total for g, k in GROUP_KEYS.items()}}
print("500 thousand abroad, " + "; ".join(f"{name}: Arab lists {scenario_matrix({**SCENARIO, 'voters_abroad': 500, 'abroad_split': split}).iloc[0][ARAB].sum():.2f}%"
                                         for name, split in bounds.items()) + f" (810 thousand: {scenario_2026[ARAB].sum():.2f}%)")

  • Fewer voters abroad barely moves the seats. With 500,000 abroad instead of 810,000, and the difference 90% other Jewish voters, other Jewish turnout of the roll rises from 71% to 75%, the Arab lists fall from 13.9% to 13.5% of the vote and keep 17 seats (the Joint List 10 instead of 11), and the Netanyahu bloc gains a seat, to 55, with a 9% chance of 61. The split is what matters: were every voter abroad an other Jewish voter, the Arab lists would fall to 13.3%; were the voters abroad spread in proportion to the rolls, every group's turnout would rise alike and no share would move. The number abroad sets how high a turnout is possible, not who wins.

The main forecast and the scenario¶

  • The Arab lists reach 13.9% of the vote and 17 seats (60% interval 15–20), against 11% and 13 in the main forecast. Arab turnout of 65.5% is two points above the 2020 record and thirteen above 2022, and the extra votes come out of every other list in proportion.
  • The Haredi lists reach 14.2% and 18 seats (Shas 10, UTJ 8), against 12.4% and 15. Turnout at the Haredi boxes of 75% is their 2013–2022 average, a point and a half above 2022, on an electorate 14% larger than 2022's; the gain is mostly growth. Other Jewish turnout at 71% is two points below 2022's.
  • The Netanyahu bloc comes out at 54 seats (51–58) with an 8% chance of 61, against 55 and 11% in the main forecast: the Haredi lists gain three seats and Likud and the Right lose about three to the rescaling. The opposition falls to 48 (45–52); with the Arab lists it reaches 66 (62–69).
  • The growth-trend electorate is close to the published 2026 roll: 2.9% above it in the Arab sector and 0.6% above it elsewhere. Using the published roll instead would take about half a seat from the Arab lists.

def bloc_table(totals):
    return pd.DataFrame({b: {"mean seats": totals[b].mean(), "median": totals[b].median(),
                             f"{INTERVAL}% interval": f"{totals[b].quantile(LOW):.0f}–{totals[b].quantile(HIGH):.0f}",
                             "P(61+)": (totals[b] >= 61).mean()}
                         for b in BLOC_ORDER + ["Opposition + Arab lists"]}).T


for name, totals in [("Main forecast (7.4)", totals_2026), ("Scenario", scenario_totals)]:
    display(bloc_table(totals).style.format({"mean seats": "{:.1f}", "median": "{:.0f}", "P(61+)": "{:.1%}"})
            .set_caption(name))


def list_table(shares, per_list):
    t = pd.DataFrame({"list": LISTS_2026["list"], "bloc": BLOC_2026, "share %": shares,
                      "mean seats": per_list["mean"], "median": per_list["median"],
                      f"{INTERVAL}% interval": [f"{lo:.0f}–{hi:.0f}" for lo, hi in zip(per_list["low"], per_list["high"])],
                      "P(pass)": per_list["P(pass)"]}, index=per_list.index)
    t["bloc"] = pd.Categorical(t["bloc"], BLOC_ORDER)
    return (t.sort_values(["bloc", "share %"], ascending=[True, False])
             .style.format({"share %": "{:.1f}", "mean seats": "{:.1f}", "median": "{:.0f}", "P(pass)": "{:.0%}"})
             .hide(axis="index"))


display(list_table(blended_2026, per_list_2026).set_caption("Main forecast (7.4)"))
